description: The popular-mods test pack (2026-11-12, replacing SIFTEC's suite): Create Fly with Flywheel, JEI, Xaero's Minimap, a GeckoLib mod, Terralith, Continuity, Mod Menu, Jade, Farmer's Delight and Traveler's Backpack. Offered when Create is loaded; a scene that needs another of them names it.

scenes.title: Xaero's Minimap in the corner over a platform of coloured blocks, HUD on, creative, empty hand (test pack)
setup: item replace entity @a weapon.mainhand with minecraft:air
scenes.requiresNote: Xaero's Minimap draws the minimap; without it the scene is the HUD over a platform.
scenes.ciNote: The pack suite's first scene and the only one with the HUD on: the next scene presses F1 (vanilla's hide-GUI key), which stays in effect for the rest of the session, so the minimap's tiles (which differ with what it has scanned) show nowhere else. Its terrain is the saved world's (pack-world.sh generates every scene area), and the platform is rebuilt the same way in every run.

scenes.title: GeckoLib entities: six of Untitled Duck Mod's geese on grass, AI off, each facing its own way (test pack)
scenes.requiresNote: The ducks are a GeckoLib mod's entities (Untitled Duck Mod, with GeckoLib).
scenes.ciNote: GeckoLib draws its baked models through the entity path (design doc, GeckoLib models: unchanged). The game is frozen (/tick freeze) before the geese are summoned, so they never tick: their age, and with it GeckoLib's animation time, is the same in every run (the suite's preamble unfreezes it for the next scene). AI off and silent besides. F1 here hides the GUI for the rest of the session (minimap tiles out of every later scene). Each goose's look is given in its summon data (Variant 0 to 2; LeftHanded off): Untitled Duck Mod otherwise picks it at random (runs 43106805198 to 43149509101; the key read from a goose's NBT, run 10f065f's tellraw).

scenes.title: The survival inventory with JEI's item list and bookmarks beside it (test pack)
setup: execute in minecraft:overworld run setblock 2280 239 -1997 minecraft:stone
item replace entity @a hotbar.0 with minecraft:diamond_pickaxe
item replace entity @a hotbar.1 with create:shaft 8
item replace entity @a inventory.0 with minecraft:oak_log 32
item replace entity @a inventory.1 with create:andesite_alloy 16
scenes.requiresNote: JEI's overlay: without it this is the plain inventory.
scenes.ciNote: Survival (peaceful, so nothing hurts), a few fixed items in fixed slots; JEI's item list on its first page. The mouse is parked in the top-left corner, where no tooltip shows. Standing on one stone block and looking up at another, each in a section other than the camera's (so Quicksilver draws terrain here too, and leaves out the faces that point away: in the camera's own section it can't).
scenes.ciStrictMaskNote: The inventory's player model (its box, 514-616 x 206-352): its pose follows the player's age (arm sway), which differs between vanilla's own runs (run 43127438207: vanilla a and b differ there by up to ~1,100 pixels); the 8/255 check covers it. The player stands on a stone block, placed before survival is switched on (without it the player fell to the ground and died, run 43136851909, and every later scene ran on the death screen), and the hotbar holds plain items.

scenes.title: Create's Ponder index screen (Create Fly's /ponder index), looking up at the sky and a stone block (package 7; test pack)
scenes.requiresNote: Create's Ponder screens come with Create (Create Fly in the test pack).
scenes.ciNote: Opened with Create's client command, typed in chat in every run (drive.py's ciChat). The index lists every item with a Ponder scene; the scenes themselves keep moving, so the index is the Ponder screen CI checks. Spectator, looking up: sky behind the screen and one stone block above the camera, so Quicksilver has terrain to draw here too (CI requires it in every scene).

scenes.title: Terralith's terrain from 30 blocks over the ground at 600 300, looking out over it (test pack)
setup: execute in minecraft:overworld positioned 600.5 0 300.5 positioned over motion_blocking run tp @a ~ ~30 ~ 45 20
scenes.requiresNote: Terralith's worldgen; without it this is vanilla terrain.
scenes.ciNote: Terrain from the saved world (pack-world.sh generates the area); mobs sent away so none walks into the shot.

scenes.title: Continuity's connected textures: walls of glass, sandstone, bookshelves, stacked glass panes and stained glass, each beside stone, and a glass floor patch (test pack)
scenes.requiresNote: Continuity's built-in Default Connected Textures and Glass Pane Culling Fix packs (enabled in every pack session's options.txt by ci/client-run.sh).
scenes.ciNote: Continuity draws its connected textures through the Fabric Renderer API (its own baked models' emitBlockQuads), so these blocks go through Quicksilver's renderer in Quicksilver's runs and Indigo in vanilla's, like Create's connected textures (create_ct). The GUI is hidden (the geckolib scene's F1).

scenes.title: Create connected textures: walls of andesite casing (with a corner), brass casing, copper casing with a stone block set in it, and framed glass, each beside a non-connecting block (stone, glass) (package 4; test pack)
scenes.requiresNote: Create's casings and framed glass: without Create the scene would show only stone, so it is skipped.
scenes.ciNote: The design doc's done-when names Create's connected textures: Create draws them through the Fabric Renderer API, so these blocks are tessellated by Quicksilver's renderer in Quicksilver's runs and by Indigo in the vanilla runs. CT blocks in view: create:andesite_casing (a 5x4 wall plus a 3-block return at its west end), create:brass_casing (a 5x4 wall and a 3x3 floor patch in front), create:copper_casing (a 5x4 wall with minecraft:stone set in at its centre left), create:framed_glass (a 5x4 wall); each wall ends against minecraft:stone or minecraft:glass, which do not connect. The GUI is hidden (the geckolib scene's F1, earlier in this session).

scenes.ciStrictMaskNote: The standing train's carriage (package 5): it lands a fraction of a pixel to one side from run to run, in vanilla's own runs too (up to 78 strict pixels in a vanilla stand-in, run 41633272149; a pin of its client-side track points did not change it), so its rectangle is out of the strict checks; the 8/255 check covers it.
scenes.requiresNote: Create's machines (Create Fly in the test pack). The belt and the train are made with /qsci, CI's pin mod's command (Create has no command for either); without it the scene shows the shafts where the belt would be and the station without a train.
scenes.ciNote: Built once per session (marker: bedrock at 2140 236 -2018; a bench's setup again only moves the camera). Create's animation clock and Flywheel's frame time are held in this area by CI's pin mod, vanilla and Quicksilver alike, so shafts, cogs, the fan, the mixer and the belt are at the same phase in every run; the clockwork bearing's hand stops at the hour (time held at 6000). What draws them: Flywheel's instances where its backend is on (indirect on the full profile), vanilla's block-entity and entity renderers where it is off (old GPU: instancing's shaders don't compile on GL 3.3 and Flywheel falls back, as in vanilla's run; Vulkan: Flywheel needs OpenGL). The GUI is hidden (the geckolib scene's F1, earlier in this session).

scenes.title: The kinetics scene with Flywheel's backend forced to instancing and Quicksilver's occlusion on still camera (package 5)
scenes.ciMedianReportOnlyNote: As factory_flat (Andre, 2026-11-01; open bug in docs/progress.md, package 4c): this session meshes a few hundred sections, mostly air (the platform floats high above the terrain), where Quicksilver's mesher is a little slower than vanilla's per section (run 41591531215: 1.478 against 1.398 ms, 165 pairs); its median is reported, not gated. For Andre to confirm (package 5).
scenes.ciStrictMaskNote: The standing train's carriage (package 5): it lands a fraction of a pixel to one side from run to run, in vanilla's own runs too (up to 78 strict pixels in a vanilla stand-in, run 41633272149; a pin of its client-side track points did not change it), so its rectangle is out of the strict checks; the 8/255 check covers it.
scenes.requiresNote: Create's machines (Create Fly in the test pack); the platform is built by the kinetics scene in the first session.
scenes.ciNote: Its own client session, with Create Fly's config/flywheel-client.json set to backend flywheel:instancing, in vanilla's runs and Quicksilver's alike, so Flywheel's instancing backend draws the same machines, contraption and train as the kinetics scene (whose session leaves Flywheel to choose: indirect on the full profile). Quicksilver's occlusion is set to still camera here (the school laptop's path: Intel picks instancing and still camera): while Flywheel holds any visual, still camera builds no pyramid and culls nothing (package 5, for Andre to decide), so on the full profile this checks that nothing is culled wrongly; on old GPU and Vulkan (Flywheel off) still camera culls and its per-frame check runs. On GL 3.3 (old GPU) instancing's shaders don't compile and Flywheel falls back to off, as in vanilla's run; on Vulkan Flywheel is off. GUI shown here (its own session): F1 hides it, as in kinetics.

scenes.requiresNote: Create's machines (Create Fly in the test pack); the platform is built by the kinetics scene in the first session.
scenes.ciNote: Its own client session (options.txt ao:false), in vanilla's runs and Quicksilver's alike. GUI hidden with F1 (its own session).
